transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time or anything. 

I guess what really made me come in is... well, I've been having a bit of a hard time at work lately. I'm a retail buyer, and I just... I can't shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of our vendors, are tracking my buys and, like, intentionally messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. 

I know it probably sounds silly to say out loud. My supervisor even sat me down and showed me the reports to prove that's not what's happening, and I want to believe him, I really do, but the feeling just won't go away. I'm sorry, does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you been feeling this way about your coworkers and vendors tracking and sabotaging your work—days, weeks, or months?

Um... well, it's been going on for a while, to be honest. I'd say roughly ten months now? I really tried to just ignore it for a long time, hoping it would go away, because I didn't want to cause any trouble or, you know, seem paranoid. 

And... um, I didn't mention this before because it's kind of embarrassing, but... around the same time, I started hearing a voice, too. Just sometimes. I hope that's okay to share, I know it sounds really bad. But yeah, the suspicious feelings and the voice... it's been about ten months. Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
During these past ten months, have you also noticed periods where your mood was very low, hopeless, or unusually high and energetic, separate from the suspicious feelings and the voice?

Um... yes, actually. I hope it's alright that I didn't say that right away. I just didn't want to overwhelm you with too much at once. 

But, um, yes. There was a time, a few months ago, where I felt... really, really good. Like, unusually good. I had all this energy, I hardly needed to sleep, and I felt like I was practically running the whole market. I was getting so much done, which I thought was a good thing at first. But then that kind of faded, and I had a stretch where things were a lot calmer. I was sleeping normally again and not feeling so... intense. 

But the thing is, even during that calmer stretch, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys. And... I was still hearing the voice in the stockroom sometimes. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it makes me sound a little... erratic. I hope that makes sense.

Outside of that period of unusually high energy and the calmer stretch afterward, was there a time—say at least a couple of weeks—when you had the suspicious feelings and heard the voice but your mood was completely normal, not elevated or low?

Um... yes, actually. I think I might have just mentioned that, but I want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much and wasting your time. 

But yeah, during that calmer stretch... when my sleep went back to normal and I didn't feel like I was, you know, running the whole market anymore... my mood felt pretty normal. Not too high, not depressed or anything. But even then, for a few weeks, I still had that strong feeling that people were tracking my buys to mess with me. And I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom. 

So, yes, there was definitely a time when my mood was completely fine, but the other stuff was still happening. Did I explain that right? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.

latest_inference.note: Confirmed a distinct manic-like episode (elevated mood, decreased sleep, increased energy) during the same illness period, plus a separate stretch of at least a couple of weeks with persistent paranoid delusions and auditory hallucinations while mood was clearly euthymic. This pattern—mood episode overlapping with psychosis, plus psychotic symptoms persisting without mood disturbance for a substantial period—fits schizoaffective disorder better than schizophrenia alone, so F20.0 is ruled out in favor of F25.0 (bipolar type).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a continuous ~10-month illness featuring persistent persecutory delusions (belief that coworkers/vendors are sabotaging her work) and auditory hallucinations (a voice in the stockroom). During this period, she also experienced a distinct manic episode (elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, increased energy, grandiosity about 'running the market') lasting more than a week, meeting full mood episode criteria concurrent with psychotic symptoms. Critically, she also had a period of at least two weeks in which the psychotic symptoms (delusions and hallucinations) persisted in the absence of any mood episode (mood was 'completely normal'), fulfilling the requirement that psychotic symptoms occur independent of mood disturbance for a substantial portion of the illness. This combination—concurrent mood episode and psychosis, plus psychosis without mood symptoms for ≥2 weeks, within a single continuous illness—is diagnostic of Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than Schizophrenia (F20.9, which would require psychosis without mood symptoms predominating) or a primary Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (F31.5, which would not account for psychosis persisting after mood symptoms resolved).
